title: mtf-facts stats record
description: Where one run spent its time and memory, written to the file --stats-file names. Times are integer nanoseconds and sizes integer bytes, so the records of many calls sum exactly; max_rss_bytes is a peak, so take the maximum. The record holds no path of an input tree.

outcome.description: completed: the command wrote its report, findings or not. error: it exited 2. timeout: its own timeout ended the run; phases may then be partial, and depth still exits 0.

exit_code.description: The exit code of the run, the same as without --stats-file.

started_unix_ns.description: When the command started, so a host can tell a stale file from this run's.

wall_ns.description: From the start of the command to the record.

cpu_user_ns.description: Process user CPU time; null where the system reports none.

cpu_system_ns.description: Process system CPU time; null where the system reports none.

max_rss_bytes.description: Peak resident set size of the process in bytes; null where the system reports none.

heap_alloc_bytes.description: Go heap bytes allocated during the run, freed or not.

files_read.description: Regular files read from input trees, counted once per read; a tree read twice counts twice.

phases.description: The steps of the run in order. They do not overlap, so their wall_ns sum to about wall_ns. The first is run, which lasts until the command starts a named step.

cpu_ns.description: Process CPU time, user and system, during the phase. Unlike wall_ns it does not grow while the process waits for a busy machine. null where the system reports none.

parse.description: Every parse of the .tf files of one directory, summed. Its time is also inside the phase each parse ran in.

rules.description: Each rule evaluated, summed over every area, sorted by id; empty for a command other than lint. Their time is also inside the rules phase.
